title: DataFlowBench case v2
description: A canonical, analyzer-neutral case. It describes flows and nonflows without naming an analyzer; native rules, models, and commands belong under adapters/<tool>/.

schema_version.description: Case schema version. A freeze binds this value as benchmark.case_schema_version and rejects a mixed-version corpus.

id.description: Stable, unique case identity — by convention dfb-<track>-<language>-<scenario>-<polarity>. It is the key that results, freeze records, and claim exclusions refer to.

template_id.description: Language-neutral semantic scenario shared by its positive and negative cases. Template IDs are immutable benchmark identities: never renamed, split, merged, or reused after retirement.

polarity.description: Whether the case asserts that flow exists (positive: reached is a true positive) or that it does not (negative: not-reached is a true negative). Every scored core template has exactly one of each per language and model profile.

negative_mechanism.description: Why the negative case does not flow: an unrelated value at the sink, a killing overwrite, field/object separation, a calling context the case never exercises, an infeasible guard, or a sanitizer on the path. Required on negative cases, forbidden on positive ones; reports break results out by this mechanism.

score_tier.description: Calibration cases validate adapters but never contribute to correctness scores. Modeling cases score the benchmark-controlled taint-modeling matrix on their own tier and never enter a core denominator. Language-extension and real-project cases have their own scorecards and never change the cross-language core denominator.

track.description: The semantic track the case belongs to. A frozen report binds exactly one track, all of its cases must match it, and tracks are never pooled.

language.description: The fixture language. Each language is a separate result population with its own core denominator; a runner never mixes two.

semantic_dimensions.description: The analysis capabilities the case exercises. Reports publish true-positive and false-positive rates per semantic dimension, and headline rates macro-average over templates and then over these dimensions.

feature_tags.description: Structural properties of the fixture, read by adapters to make capability decisions before invocation. A preregistered partition reads only feature_tags and expected_analysis_capability — never an observed result — so no case can move between the scored and unsupported partitions after the fact.

model_profile.description: Whether DataFlowBench supplies equivalent models or evaluates models shipped by the tool. Results from the two profiles are never combined.

fixture_files.description: Fixture source files, relative to the case directory. The corpus fixture revision hashes each declared filename with its bytes, so this list is part of the corpus identity.

source_anchors.description: Where the tainted value originates. Normalized results copy these anchors verbatim, and only anchor-backed evidence may become reached.

sink_anchors.description: Where the value must (or must not) arrive. A tool finding matches when its own evidence reconciles to the anchored sink in the anchor file, never by adapter guesswork.

expected_flows.description: Source-to-sink pairs the case asserts do reach. Non-empty on positive cases, empty on negatives.

expected_nonflows.description: Source-to-sink pairs the case asserts do not reach. Non-empty on negative cases.

witness_checkpoints.description: Ordered DFB- markers a complete witness path must visit; each must occur exactly once across the fixture files. Result normalizers never synthesize them — a result carries a checkpoint only when the tool actually reported it.

expected_analysis_capability.description: The named capability an engine needs to answer this case, read together with feature_tags by preregistered partitions to decide unsupported before the tool is invoked.

kind.description: Free-form capability identifier (e.g. heap-field-sensitive-taint, reflective-dispatch-taint). Deliberately not enum-constrained so new tiers can extend the vocabulary; the values in use are fixed per template in the preregistration documents.

execution_budget.description: The analysis budget the case is authored against — not the observed wall clock; an over-budget run is reported rather than silently rebudgeted.

wall_clock_seconds.description: Wall-clock seconds allotted for the analysis.

fixture_provenance.description: Licensing and origin record for the fixture — part of the public benchmark contract, not optional metadata. See docs/fixture-provenance.md.

kind.description: Authored fixtures are original DataFlowBench code; imported fixtures are copied from a named upstream project at an immutable revision and keep their original license.

origin.description: DataFlowBench for authored fixtures; the upstream project for imported ones.

revision.description: The introducing revision for authored fixtures, or the upstream immutable revision or release for imported ones.

license.description: MIT for authored executable fixtures; otherwise the retained upstream license.

tool_model_references.description: Per-tool map naming the committed rule, query, or model artifact the case is run against — or the retained reason a tool declines it. Canonical cases never contain native rule syntax; adapters that resolve models globally rather than per case carry no key here, and tool-native cases carry an empty map because a native run loads only what the vendor ships.

policy.description: Path to the tool's committed policy file for this case.

query.description: Path to the tool's committed query for this case.

unsupported_reason.description: Verbatim, retained rationale for why this tool declines the case, emitted as unsupported rather than a negative result.

marker.description: The DFB-SOURCE:/DFB-SINK: comment marker text, which must appear verbatim in the named fixture file; runners resolve endpoints by reading these marker lines out of the fixture itself.

file.description: The fixture file containing the marker; must be one of fixture_files.

line_hint.description: Optional 1-based line the marker sits on. Validation fails if the marker is not on the hinted line, so a hint is an assertion, not documentation.

source.description: A DFB-SOURCE: marker declared in source_anchors, naming the origin endpoint of the asserted (non)flow.

sink.description: A DFB-SINK: marker declared in sink_anchors, naming the destination endpoint of the asserted (non)flow.
